title: Hong Kong privacy commissioner investigates OneDegree data breach that may affect 約11萬人
date_note: The PCPD says it received OneDegree's breach notification on 19 November; RTHK published on 24 November.
geo_basis: Only Hong Kong is stated; pinned at the territory's centre
summary: RTHK reports that Hong Kong's Privacy Commissioner (PCPD) received OneDegree's breach notification on 19 November and, on preliminary information, says it may affect 約11萬人. OneDegree said some customers' ID cards and a few customers' bank account numbers were stolen by unauthorised persons, and that credit card data was not involved. The PCPD has opened an investigation.
plain: Hong Kong's privacy watchdog is investigating a breach at OneDegree that may affect 約11萬人. OneDegree says some ID cards and a few bank account numbers were stolen, but not credit card data.
exec: The PCPD says the OneDegree breach may affect 約11萬人, and it has opened an investigation.
action: OneDegree advises customers to be alert to suspicious calls, texts, emails and links.
impact: PCPD preliminary information says possibly names, ID card numbers, photos, dates of birth and financial information.

evidence.quote: 私隱專員公署表示，本月19日接獲虛擬保險公司OneDegree的資料外洩事故通報，初步資料顯示，可能影響約11萬人的個人資料
部分客戶資料被未經授權人士非法盜取，涉及部分客戶的身份證及少數客戶的銀行戶口號碼，但不涉及信用卡資料。

validation.note: Only RTHK was read, quoting the PCPD and OneDegree; the PCPD's own statement and OneDegree's notice were not found by search.
